traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report presents two parallel result sets for the sensitivity/method-comparison study: 'Individual samples' (Table 5) and 'Pooled samples' (Table 6). I recorded the Individual samples table (Table 5) as the primary/canonical dataset since it is presented first and is the standard single-sample protocol; the Pooled samples values (Table 6) are very similar (e.g. Composite foods SEalt 78.1/SEref 78.1/AC 83.1/FP 0.0; Meat products 97.0/78.8/88.7/2.6; Milk & Dairy 76.7/76.7/83.5/5.5; Vegetables 81.3/71.9/76.9/6.1; Fish and seafood 93.5/90.3/92.9/0.0; Environmental samples 73.3/83.3/82.7/4.4) but were not recorded per-category to avoid duplication. The interlaboratory study (section 4) reports separate overall Single/Pooling protocol sensitivities (not broken down by category) and an RLOD table with an Acceptability Limit of 2.5 (not a bias/trueness acceptability limit in log units, since this is a qualitative method, so acceptability_limit_log field is not applicable and quantitative block is null). Category names taken exactly as printed (with numbering symbols removed to plain text) from Table 5/7.
